scope: Michigan Avenue to Lake Michigan, just north of 16th Street to Cermak Road: the Prairie Avenue district as the Sanborn 1911 sheets 20, 28 and 35 and the Robinson 1886 plate draw it, the Illinois Central right-of-way on its made ground, and the lake beyond it.
standard: No survey of 1904 levels in this reach has been found. The grade is read off the MODERN ground where the modern street is the 1911 one, and it is inferred to be the 1904 grade only where houses of the period still stand on it at their own grade (research zone 3). Everywhere else it is reconstructed, and no land elevation here is attested.

context.label: Zero
context.text: Z = 0.0 ft at the summer-1835 lake and river water surface (data/datum.json)

context.label: The modelled box
context.text: 700 x 900 m at 2.5 m cells (the e1834 box's own cell), 281 x 361 samples; the shoreline file spans it.

context.label: Measured relief
context.text: Land in the modelled box runs 0.0 to 15.1 ft above the water surface, and the channel floor reaches -7.996 ft below it. Measured from the committed heightfield, not asserted.

claims.label: lake_surface
notes: Research zone 2. No 1904 lake stage has been found. The water stands at the 1835 plane, Z = 0, so the two scenes' water is one level; the terrain dossier's historic range of 576-582 ft (Z -4 to +2) bounds it, and a stage record for 1904 would replace it.
